brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb (center cell with 6 surrounding cells on one level)
requirements.evidence: Placed 7 full bases at 0,0,0 plus q,r: -1,0 / -1,1 / 0,-1 / 0,1 / 1,-1 / 1,0 forming complete honeycomb; get_build counts 7 pieces.

requirements.requirement: Standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet
requirements.evidence: Three stud spikes facing down installed at junctions: spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0 and spike:0#-1,0|0,-1|0,0 and spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 (s20,s21,s23); additional 3 stud-down positions available on same honeycomb.

finish.summary: Built 7-cell honeycomb (center + 6 neighbours) on level 0, capped open faces and locked joints. Installed 3 stud spikes facing down at three different triple-junctions as feet; build passes check_build with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your honeycomb on stud-spike feet — I'll build it now.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: I've got your seven-cell honeycomb mapped — now I'll assemble it and fit those stud-spike feet.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.
